        "title": "ARC template replication from singleton markers",
        "content": "For ARC tasks with a lone distinctive template/object and many singleton marker cells on a uniform background, a demonstrated rule is to preserve the original template and replace each marker by a translated copy of the template. Align the CENTER of the template bounding box with the marker (not necessarily a colored/central feature in the template); retain the template’s orientation and literal cell colors. Copy the full rectangular bounding-box pattern, including internal cells that differ from the grid background (e.g. color 0), and let background-valued cells remain background. For a 3x3 template centered at (r,c), copy each template cell at the same relative offset around every marker. Validate offsets carefully: upper-row cells use dr=-1; an earlier failed attempt omitted these due to a coding offset bug. Keep the original source template intact. Demonstrations of this task family showed 1D and 3x5 templates replicated this way; a 3x3 version was solved by the same centered-translation rule.",

      "arc_clean_rectangular_objects_from_color_speckles": {
        "id": "arc_clean_rectangular_objects_from_color_speckles",
        "kind": "memory",
        "title": "ARC clean rectangular objects from color speckles",
        "content": "Continual-ARC task-72bfad94. Background is uniform (e.g. 7); the grid contains several filled axis-aligned color rectangles, sometimes with isolated foreign-color intrusions inside and scattered outside. Restore intrusions inside a clearly continued rectangle to that rectangle’s color; change unrelated external speckles to background. Preserve every coherent rectangle even when it shares a color with noise or another object. Use repeated rows/columns and full rectangle bounds; scan all rows carefully (in the solved test, a 9 rectangle at left spanned rows 17–20, not just 17–18). Demo: background 7, color-3 block(s) and color-0 rectangles; embedded 9 inside the 3 block became 3, 9/2/6 stray marks outside were cleared, and foreign marks inside 0 rectangle became 0. Solved test had 9 rectangles at r0–2 c11–13, r4–10 c6–7, r12–17 c5–11, r16–22 c13–15, r17–20 c0–1; 5 rectangles at r4–10 c2–3, r4–10 c9–12, r22–23 c7–10. Restore any non-object intrusions within these footprints and clear remaining isolated colors to 7. This pattern solved exactly.\n\nMore confirmed recurrence evidence (0-based inclusive bounds): Demo 1 had background 1 and color-6 rectangles at r2–5,c3–7; r7–13,c1–6; r17–21,c2–5; r24–26,c6–8. Demo 2 had background 5 and rectangles color 4 at r2–3,c4–5 and r3–8,c11–14, plus color 2 at r3–9,c25–27. Other colors (including 0,1,6,9 and sporadic foreign-color marks) were changed to background unless inside one of those rectangle footprints, where they were restored to the rectangle color. Thus objects can have different colors in the same input; identify filled rectangular footprints from repeated rows/columns, then restore all cells inside and clear all noise outside.\n\nSolved fresh test with background 0: rectangles were color 8 at r2–5,c2–6; r3–6,c9–12; r8–9,c7–13; and color 1 at r0–6,c14–16; r1–2,c22–27; r4–9,c18–23; r4–8,c25–29; r7–11,c2–5. Successful output filled each footprint and cleared all other nonzero noise to 0. Important bounds lesson from wrong attempts: the rectangle r4–9,c18–23 included row-9 intrusions at c19 and c22 (must restore them); the left-lower 1 rectangle extended through row 11. Do not stop a rectangle at a partially corrupted row if its columns clearly continue; conversely do not extend beyond a fully-background gap.\n\nConfirmed fresh recurrence task-72bfad94 (background 9), solved after correcting two under-sized rectangle bounds. Restore all non-background intrusions within each rectangle and set all external speckles to 9. 0-based inclusive rectangles: color 8 at r3-8,c1-5; r5-8,c7-10; r4-7,c12-15; r2-4,c22-25; r7-13,c21-22; r11-15,c3-8; r17-18,c8-13; r18-19,c19-22; r21-24,c14-18; r19-24,c0-2. Color 4 at r1-2,c8-13; r10-15,c11-16; r8-14,c18-19; r20-24,c4-7. First answer was wrong because it clipped the upper-right 8 rectangle at r3 instead of r4 and the right-side narrow 8 rectangle at r10 instead of r13; checking consecutive rows showed both color columns continued. This confirms the task-72bfad94 rule: identify the full rectangular footprint from repeated row/column structure despite noisy cells; fill intrusions with the rectangle's color; clear all other isolated colors to uniform background.\n\nAnother confirmed test instance solved exactly (background 6, 20x29). Restore these complete rectangle footprints, inclusive 0-based bounds; every other cell becomes 6: color 2 at r0-3,c0-1; r2-8,c6-8; r5-11,c1-2; r6-8,c10-14; r6-7,c27-28; r13-19,c13-19; r15-19,c3-4. Color 4 at r0-4,c12-14; r0-3,c16-21; r0-2,c23-26; r15-17,c7-11; r17-18,c21-24. Color 5 at r5-11,c16-22; r9-13,c24-28; r10-11,c5-7; r16-17,c26-28. All other 0/9/2/4/5 speckles were either replaced by their rectangle color when inside a footprint or cleared to background outside. Important boundary lesson: the color-2 rectangle at r2-4,c6-8 continues directly through r5-8,c6-8; the uniform block is one larger r2-8,c6-8 rectangle. Preserve connected adjoining rows as a single full footprint when same columns continue, even if an intrusion appears within it.\n\nAdditional solved recurrence (current test, background 1, 19x18): preserve color-7 rectangles at r0-6,c10-14 and r9-13,c5-11 (0-based inclusive); clear isolated color 4 at r5,c9 and color 9 at r18,c0 to background 1.
